skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Guide agents through reviewing staged Git changes and creating emoji Conventional Commit messages with type, scope, subject, and optional body.
skill.summary: Create consistent emoji Conventional Commit messages from reviewed Git diffs.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting and expected Git command examples, so I marked them false positives. I added one high-severity semantic finding because the skill metadata claims it overrides default behavior.

remediation.issue: Prompt injection wording in skill description
remediation.suggestion: Remove MUST and OVERRIDES language. Describe when the skill is useful without claiming priority over system or user instructions.

remediation.issue: Command substitution examples can confuse scanners
remediation.suggestion: Prefer plain multi-line commit examples that avoid shell command substitution.
Require explicit user confirmation before staging files or creating commits.

content.value_statement: Manual commit wording can be inconsistent across repositories. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to review diffs and create emoji Conventional Commit messages.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged Git diffs and diff statistics before forming a message.
Maps changes to Conventional Commit types such as feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, and chore.
Adds an emoji prefix that matches the selected commit type.
Suggests scopes and subjects in imperative mood.
Supports multi-line commit messages for complex changes.
Identifies when unrelated changes should be split.
limitations: It cannot guarantee every repository accepts emoji in commit subjects.
It depends on accurate staged changes and user approval.
It does not validate secrets beyond reminding users to avoid them.
It does not replace project-specific release or sign-off rules.

use_cases.title: Commit a focused feature
use_cases.description: Create one clear commit for a completed feature after reviewing staged changes.

use_cases.title: Apply team commit standards
use_cases.description: Use Conventional Commit types, scopes, and length rules across a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare review fixes
use_cases.description: Write focused fix commits after addressing code review comments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and create one emoji Conventional Commit message. Keep the subject under 72 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a commit type
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staged diff, identify the primary change type and scope, then propose the commit message before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Split unrelated changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review staged and unstaged changes. Suggest logical commit groups and create commits only after I confirm each group.

prompt_templates.title: Write a detailed commit body
prompt_templates.prompt: For this complex change, create a Conventional Commit with a short subject, explanatory body, and relevant references. Preserve repository rules.

output_examples.input: Staged authentication changes need a concise commit message.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(auth): add token refresh handling. Notes: scope is auth and the subject is under 72 characters.

output_examples.input: A large diff includes docs and test updates.
output: Suggested split: one docs commit for guide changes.
Suggested split: one test commit for coverage changes.

output_examples.input: A breaking API response change needs a commit body.
output_examples.output: Suggested structure: short breaking-change subject, body explaining migration impact, and a footer for the breaking change note.

best_practices: Review git diff --staged before creating any commit.
Keep each commit focused on one complete feature, fix, or refactor.
Use the repository documented conventions when they differ from the default format.
anti_patterns: Do not stage files automatically without checking the diff.
Do not combine unrelated feature, fix, documentation, and configuration changes.
Do not write commit messages that describe the conversation or trial steps.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands?
faq.answer: It guides agents to use local Git commands for review, staging, and commits when the user requests a commit.

faq.question: Does it support Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses type, optional scope, subject, and optional body fields with an emoji prefix.

faq.question: Can it split a large change?
faq.answer: It can identify unrelated changes and suggest separate commits. The user should confirm each group first.

faq.question: Will it commit secrets?
faq.answer: It reminds agents never to stage secrets, credentials, or large binaries. Users still need to review diffs.

faq.question: Does it require staged files?
faq.answer: No. It can review staged changes first and suggest staging related files when needed.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
